chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Ali, from Aban, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the slave becomes blind, his master manumits him, and it is not permissible for him to keep him."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping a blind slave in servitude according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the obligation of emancipation (ikrah) for a slave who loses their sight, as blindness renders them unable to fulfill their duties effectively. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the master cannot retain the slave in servitude once the capacity for work is lost, ensuring the slave's dignity and freedom. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of manumission within Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam, highlighting the transition from servitude to liberty based on physical capability.
